requirements.title: io-control-spec syntax enumerates unit, format, namelist, control, branch, status, position, record, and size specifiers
requirements.definition: An io-control-spec is one of the listed forms: optionally keyworded UNIT= io-unit, FMT= format, NML= namelist-group-name, ADVANCE=, ASYNCHRONOUS=, BLANK=, DECIMAL=, DELIM=, END=, EOR=, ERR=, ID=, IOMSG=, IOSTAT=, LEADING_ZERO=, PAD=, POS=, REC=, ROUND=, SIGN=, or SIZE= with the indicated expression, variable, label, or name operand. The bracketed UNIT=, FMT=, and NML= alternatives are the syntax source for omitted-keyword admission; C1211, C1218, and C1219 supply the placement restrictions.

requirements.title: ERR, EOR, and END labels are same-scope branch target statements
requirements.definition: For each ERR=, EOR=, or END= specifier, the label shall identify a branch target statement, and that branch target statement shall appear in the same inclusive scope as the data transfer statement.
requirements.oracle:
C1215 has two independent obligations for each ERR=, EOR=, and END= label: branch-target statement identity and same-inclusive-scope placement. The branch-target negatives keep the label in scope but change only the statement kind; the same-scope negatives keep a branch target statement with the label but move it outside the data transfer statement's inclusive scope. Future fixtures must compile a conforming same-scope control and must not rely on IOMSG text, branch execution, or a particular diagnostic wording.

requirements.title: Format or namelist controls make a data transfer formatted; absence makes it unformatted
requirements.definition: If the data transfer statement contains a format or namelist-group-name, the statement is a formatted input/output statement; otherwise, it is an unformatted input/output statement.

Mixed-form decision: the admission of omitted UNIT= is carried by R1213 [UNIT=] io-unit syntax; C1211 is retained as the presence and first-item restriction.

Mixed-form decision: the admission of omitted NML= is carried by R1213 [NML=] namelist syntax; C1219 is retained as positional-namelist placement restrictions.
